correctness.rationale: A complete dyadic split gives both sides of the trace asymptotic for every small radius, not merely along a subsequence. For J=floor(log_2(1/r)), the low-frequency increment is at most Jr and the tail is O(r). At the test pair 0 and r e_1, the first J normalized terms sum to J+O(1) because the quadratic sine errors are summable, while the normalized tail is O(1). For the extension, the source's uniform vertical derivative estimate contributes only O(r), and Poisson positivity contracts the horizontal boundary modulus. Boundary restriction supplies the matching lower bound.
